---
title: "Registry API"
description: "Store local simulator factories behind explicit names."
jupyter: python3
---

Most code should call an explicit design constructor. Use `DGPRegistry` when an
experiment reads design names from configuration or a separate project keeps
its own design catalog.

```{python}
import inspect

from pypanelsim import core, designs

print(inspect.signature(core.DGPRegistry))
for name in ("register", "create", "names"):
    print(name, inspect.signature(getattr(core.DGPRegistry, name)))
```

## Register a factory

A factory must return a `PanelSimulator`.

```{python}
registry = core.DGPRegistry()

def classic_small(*, overlap=0.0):
    config = designs.CanonicalPanelConfig(
        n_control=60,
        n_treated=20,
        n_pre=24,
        n_post=8,
    )
    return designs.classic_factor_design(
        config=config,
        overlap=overlap,
    )

registry.register("classic_small", classic_small)
print(registry.names())
```

Names must start with a lowercase letter and contain only lowercase letters,
digits, and underscores. Registering the same name twice raises an error unless
`replace=True` is supplied.

## Create and simulate

```{python}
simulator = registry.create("classic_small", overlap=1.0)
panel = simulator.simulate(seed=42)

print(simulator.name)
print(panel.shape)
```

`create` forwards keyword arguments to the registered factory. An unknown name
raises a key error that lists the available names.

## Keep registries local

Do not add every paper-specific experiment to the public package. A project can
define a registry next to its experiment configuration:

```python
EXPERIMENTS = core.DGPRegistry()
EXPERIMENTS.register("main_null", make_main_null)
EXPERIMENTS.register("main_power", make_main_power)
```

The functions remain ordinary Python and can be tested directly. The registry
adds lookup by name; it does not explain the scientific design.
